title: Send button not pressable by accessibility services (voice keyboard can't hit Send)
description:
The chat composer's send/stop button renders fine but is not clickable to Android accessibility services. Root cause: Semantics(excludeSemantics: true) in ChatComposer._buildSendButton drops the inner IconButton's tap action, so the merged node is a non-clickable button (label='Send message', isButton, isEnabled, no tap action). BubbleKeyboard's send finder requires clickable within 4 ancestors, so the swipe-to-send gesture can never find it.

Fix: re-declare onTap (streaming ? onStop : onSend) on the Semantics wrapper.

Discovered while wiring BubbleKeyboard's swipe-to-finish-recording-and-send flow against Hermes.

title: Show a 1–2 line live status inside each running tool call
description:
While a tool call is running, its progress UI should show a short running status: one or two lines saying what the tool is doing at that moment. Right now there is no per-step description inside the tool call.

Mock-up: **link needed.** The note asks for a link to the bead mock-up, but none is recorded in the repo or in the beads. (The only mock-up link in the beads is on the closed bead hmy-qy4, Topic icons, which is a different feature.) Add the mock-up URL here before starting work.

Where the code is today (checked in the repo):
- `lib/core/models/gateway_activity.dart`: `GatewayToolActivity` maps `tool.progress` / `tool.generating` events to a `detail` field taken from the `preview`/`detail` payload keys, and `tool.complete` takes `summary`. `_normalizeText` collapses whitespace and truncates to a maximum length, so there is already a single-line text source that could drive this.
- `lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart`: `parseSseFrame` sends `hermes.tool.progress` SSE frames to `onToolProgress`.

title: Review upstream changes from fork point to latest release and plan their inclusion
description:
Review the features and fixes that upstream has shipped between the point where hermes-android forked and upstream's latest release. Decide for each one whether hermes-android should include it, defer it or skip it. Then record the accepted changes in an openspec change named `upstream-changes`, which tracks and carries out their inclusion.

No specific upstream fixes are known to be needed yet. Finding them is part of this review.

This will happen again every time upstream publishes a new release. Each later review covers the changes between the last release we reviewed and the new one, and adds its results to the same `upstream-changes` change, so the spec grows with each cycle. This first review creates that change and also sets the baseline and the steps that future reviews will follow.

This is separate from two open beads: hmy-4fo, which proposes our theming layer to upstream (the opposite direction), and hmy-xfw, which covers the material_ui package migration. If an upstream change affects either of those, link it to that bead instead of tracking it again here.
design:
Range: from the fork point (the merge-base of our main branch with upstream) up to the tag of upstream's latest release. Record the exact fork-point commit and the release tag in the output.

Triage: list the upstream changes in that range, grouped by feature or fix rather than by commit. Give each one a decision (include, defer or skip) and a one-line reason. Changes that touch theming or material_ui are linked to hmy-4fo or hmy-xfw and are not triaged here. No upstream fixes are known to be needed in advance, so flag any urgent ones the triage turns up (for example security or crash fixes) so their items can be given a higher priority.

Planning contract: create the openspec change `upstream-changes` and add the accepted changes to it, with one tracked item per accepted change or group of related changes. Each item carries out its inclusion by merge or cherry-pick and has its own acceptance criteria. Record the reviewed range and the triage decisions in the same change so the history stays in one place.

Recurring process: record the last reviewed upstream release tag in `upstream-changes`. Write down the steps (find the range starting from that tag, triage, then extend `upstream-changes` with the newly accepted items) so the next upstream release is handled the same way, by growing the same change rather than starting a new one.
acceptance_criteria:
- The openspec change `upstream-changes` exists.
- The fork-point commit and the upstream release tag that set the reviewed range are both recorded in `upstream-changes`.
- Every upstream feature or fix in that range has a decision (include, defer or skip) and a reason. The ones that touch theming or material_ui are linked to hmy-4fo or hmy-xfw instead.
- Any urgent upstream fixes found in triage are flagged in `upstream-changes`.
- `upstream-changes` has one tracked item, with its own acceptance criteria, for each accepted change.
- The last reviewed upstream release tag is recorded in `upstream-changes`, and the repeatable steps for extending it after the next upstream release are documented.

title: Epic: Beads kanban board in hermes-android project mode
description:
Add a kanban view of beads (bd) issues to the hermes-android app as a project mode feature. When a project is open, the board reads that project's beads database through the Hermes agent or server and shows its issues. Reuse the UI and some of the AI logic from nacre where it makes sense.

This is an epic. The first child is a feasibility spike (see design). The board work comes after it and depends on what the spike finds.

Source note: "Integrate a beads kanban (maybe leveraging logic from nacre)". Owner clarifications: "Read the beads db for the project (this would be a project mode feature)". "Through the hermes agent or server. What you can, and what makes sense. Probably the UI and some of the ai logic, at your recommendation. You can make this an epic and create a spike for feasibility. I defer to you on Port vs library. Implement this in a branch and we can see how it does."

None of the existing open beads (U01–U19, upstream sync, release, theming, material_ui migration) cover this.
design:
- Scope: the board is only available in project mode and is tied to the active project. It does not aggregate across projects.
- Data path: the app does not read the beads database directly. It asks the Hermes agent or server running for the active project, and that side reads the project's beads (bd) database and returns the issues. The spike decides whether the agent or the server is the better place for this.
- Board: issues are grouped into columns by bd status.
- Read vs write: build the read-only board first. Moving cards between columns (which writes status back to bd through the agent/server) is in scope if the spike shows it can be done safely. Otherwise it gets its own follow-up bead.
- Nacre reuse: reuse nacre's kanban UI and the parts of its AI logic that fit project mode. The spike lists exactly which parts.
- Port vs library (the owner left this to me): port the needed nacre code into hermes-android rather than adding nacre as a dependency. That keeps the app's build and release free of an external coupling, and we only need part of nacre. Switch to a shared library only if the spike finds nacre can already be consumed as a package from the app's stack without much extra work.
- Children:
  1. Spike: feasibility (time-boxed). Outputs: (a) whether the agent or the server can return the active project's bd issues, and roughly what that interface looks like; (b) whether bd status writes through that path are feasible; (c) a list of the nacre UI and AI logic to reuse, with a confirmed port-or-library decision; (d) a go/no-go recommendation.
  2. Read-only project-mode board (after the spike).
  3. Card moves / status write-back (only if the spike finds it feasible).
- Branching: do all implementation on a dedicated feature branch. Don't merge it to main until the owner has tried it and accepted it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A spike child bead exists and is closed with written findings covering the agent-vs-server data path, bd write feasibility, the nacre reuse list, the port-or-library decision and a go/no-go.
- The work is on a dedicated feature branch and is not merged to main without the owner's sign-off.
- In project mode, a kanban view shows the beads issues from the active project's beads database, fetched through the Hermes agent or server.
- Issues are grouped into columns by bd status. Each card shows at least the issue ID and title.
- The board is not offered outside project mode.
- Switching to a different project shows that project's issues and none from the previous project.
- If the project has no beads database, or the agent/server can't reach or read it, the view shows a clear empty or error state and does not crash.
- If write-back ships: moving a card updates the issue's status in bd through the agent/server, the board reflects the stored status after a refresh, and a failed write is shown to the user and reverts the card.
notes:
Implementation underway in existing detached worktree under injected no-Git session rule. Feasibility corrected: inline Python is blocked by Hermes safety, so shipped design is a typed projects.beads RPC with a companion server adapter; never evade shell policy.
